order: Make the review engine selectable through a single configuration key in the project settings file, so the choice of which engine judges a review lives in one place rather than being hardcoded. Support at minimum a default engine, an alternate cross-vendor engine with a fallback to the default when the alternate is unavailable, and a dual mode where both engines review substantively and a coordinating role arbitrates between them. Keep both engines installed under one contract regardless of which is selected, so swapping the key must only ever change who judges — it must never change what gets checked — and an in-conversation instruction still overrides the setting for that session. Grant the coordinating role a narrow read carve-out for the settings file itself, since read access there was never guard-blocked in the first place; this is documented permission only, not a change to any existing guard. Update the review-routing logic to honor the setting and document the key and the swap flow in the project's top-level documentation.
claims: The engine choice was moved into a single configuration key supporting a default engine, an alternate cross-vendor engine with fallback to the default when unavailable, and a dual mode with arbitration; swapping the key changes only who judges, never what gets checked. A narrow read carve-out for the settings file was added to existing role law — read access was never guard-blocked there — and the review-routing logic and top-level documentation were updated to match, across two files with 12 insertions and 3 deletions.
